newsitem.title: UK: Brent crude moves up in thin physical trade.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude moves up in thin physical trade.

text.p: Brent crude crept higher with the last reported deal seen seven cents higher than Monday's levels but North Seea physical activity was thin although sentiment remained firm, traders said.
Brent outright values were softer in sympathy with falling screen prices. January futures traded 15 cents lower in the afternoon, having dipped earlier to $23.35 a barrel.
But Brent CFDs made a determined move up, with next week's dates bid three cents higher after a trader kept today's Dec 18-20 Brent date and sold it on to another trader at January +42 cents.
The second set of dates was also believed to have been kept by a trading house.
This was seven cents higher than the last reported Brent deals on Monday, when at least four cargoes were sold although North Sea physical trades have generally been scarce in the last week.
Traders were sceptical of remarks by an Iraqi official that Iraqi oil exports could restart next week, but one said an additional 500,000 barrels per day (bpd) was unlikely to depress prices.
"Do people really care? It seems to be that with overall consumption of 75 million barrels a day, an additional half a million barrels is not a major point," a trader for a European oil company said.
Iraq is expected to export 500,000-700,000 bpd of crude under its "oil-for-food" deal with the United Nations.
Traders saw the Elf refinery strikes in France having much more impact on the market by making available additional barrels previously thought to have found homes.
Unions and managers at Elf Aquitaine agreed on Tuesday to hold concrete negotiations to end the dispute.
